Package io.mavlink4j.codec

Class FrameReader

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.codec.FrameReader
public final class FrameReader extends Object
Bytes in, frames out. Delegates all real parsing (CRC, resync-past-garbage, dialect-specific field layout) to io.dronefleet.mavlink — this class's only job is bridging the incremental ByteChunks a MavlinkLink produces into that library's frame decoder, one independent ResyncBuffer per source.

One resync buffer per source

For a boundary-preserving link (MavlinkLink.preservesMessageBoundaries() true — UDP), each distinct LinkPeer gets its own buffer. For a stream link (false — TCP) every chunk shares exactly one buffer regardless of what ByteChunk.source() reports, since a stream link has exactly one logical byte sequence by construction. This is not an optimisation: concatenating datagrams from different vehicles into one byte stream splices one sender's partial frame onto another's and corrupts both, which is exactly what rules out a single shared buffer on a datagram link. Buffers are bounded and evicted least-recently-used at MavlinkSettings.maxResyncBuffers() so a spoofing or scanning source cannot grow memory without bound.

This is where received time is decided: a ByteChunk carries none, so every Frame (and every SignatureRejection) is stamped from MavlinkSettings.clock().

Not thread-safe: intended to be driven by exactly one reader thread per link (matching L3's MavlinkSession, which owns one reader thread per link), the same "one thread owns the read side" convention every link implementation in io.mavlink4j.transport follows.

    • offer

      public void offer(ByteChunk chunk, Consumer<Frame> out)
      Feeds chunk's bytes into that source's resync buffer and hands every frame that becomes fully decodable as a result to out, in order. May decode zero, one, or several frames from a single chunk; never blocks.
